faq.q: Can I photograph jewelry without hiring a model?
faq.a: Yes. One sharp photo can become a tight close-up, a worn frame, or a styled scene. The bracelet on the wrist starts from the photo you already have.

faq.q: Will the stones and the metal color stay true?
faq.a: They follow the stones and the metal color in your photo. Even light gives the truest tone, and a sharp source keeps the setting readable.

faq.q: Can a flat lay of a necklace become a worn photo?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for a close frame at the collarbone and a plain neckline. An AI avatar wears it. Keep the frame on the chain and the pendant.

faq.q: Can a phone photo of a tiny ring work?
faq.a: Yes, when the source is sharp and the ring fills the frame. Wipe dust and fingerprints first, and use even light instead of a flash on the metal.

faq.q: Will this cover bags, watches, and sunglasses?
faq.a: Yes. Show the clasp and the metal parts up close, then show the item carried or worn so the size reads at once. Sunglasses on a face do that in one frame.

faq.q: How do I suggest ring size without printing numbers on the photo?
faq.a: Set the ring beside a familiar coin or card, or on an adult hand. The exact inner size, and the sizes you sell, still belong in the listing text.

faq.q: Which frame should I use for a gallery and a story?
faq.a: Use a sharp square close-up for the gallery. For a story, make a tall worn or unboxing scene at 9:16.

faq.q: Can these files run as paid jewelry ads?
faq.a: Yes. Files download without a watermark, so you can use them in paid ads and on listings. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits.

faq.q: Can I begin from a product link and make several versions?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the product page, or send it from your shop software through the API. Ask for the bracelet on a wrist in one version and flat on linen in the other.

reviews.h2: How Jewelry Brands Switch to AI Ads
reviews.lead: Example ways jewelry and accessory sellers use one photo. These are not quotes.

items.t: Close-up, then a coin for size
items.d: They upload a sharp top view and ask for a tight close-up. A second photo places a coin beside the band. The size inside the ring stays in the listing.

items.t: Flat chain to a worn close-up
items.d: One flat photo becomes a tight worn photo with a plain neckline. They count the stones and the links before they list it.
They ask for both studs in a tight photo and reject a result that changes the pin or the metal color.
A close photo shows the clasp, and a shoulder photo shows the size. The person is created by the tool.

items.t: Gift scene from the same photo
items.d: The piece sits in a simple gift scene for a social post, while the listing image stays a clean close-up of the real design.
They show the glasses on a head only from their own photo. They do not ask for a logo they do not own.

items.t: A link, then a short line
items.d: They paste the product page. Or they send that link from their own shop software (the API). They ask for a short script about the piece. Size and care stay out of the spoken line.
They pick a person the tool creates for a wrist or collarbone photo. Then they make a second version of that person. They check the stone count first.
They choose a voice, or a short sample of their own. They check the captions, pick a music track, and trim the clip in the editor before export.
They make the worn clip again in a second language from the same photo. Metal color and stone count still have to match the real piece.
They type a description of the piece in the text box and keep a few versions. They send the one they want to TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram. The listing photo stays a clean close-up.
